title: Experiment — one research question over one workload version with N variants

metric_glossary_entry.description: Human-readable meaning of one metric this experiment reports. Direction is never assumed for an unknown metric: an entry must state it.

interpretation.description: How to read a value in context (e.g. what 0.5 or 1.0 means for a ranking metric).

datasets.description: Named datasets this chart references. Each must be one of the experiment's own named_datasets — never a URL data source.

research_question.description: The question this experiment exists to answer, distinct from hypothesis (the proposed answer). Immutable scientific meaning, owned here rather than in any run manifest.

primary_outcomes.description: Pre-registered metric names the experiment is judged on. Each must be a named_dataset and must have a metric_glossary entry (enforced by validate()).

success_criteria.description: What result would support the hypothesis, stated before execution.

falsification_criteria.description: What result would falsify the hypothesis, stated before execution.

non_claims.description: What this experiment explicitly does not establish.

metric_glossary.description: Metric name (a named_datasets value) to its human-readable meaning, direction and unit.

terminology.description: Canonical vocabulary this experiment uses (e.g. System One, Jev, Noul, Choice, Score), term to definition. Durable evidence uses TypeSafe terminology; this map is what the UI shows.

named_datasets.description: The complete set of named (non-URL) datasets this experiment's chart_specs may reference — usually metric names.

legend.description: Maps every named dataset and variant id used by this experiment to a human-readable label. Completeness is enforced by validate(), not by this schema alone.

statuses.description: Domain-specific status vocabulary this object uses, if any. Each value must have a legend entry.

label_values.description: Domain-specific label vocabulary this object uses, if any (e.g. choice-question option values). Each value must have a legend entry.
